title: Boeuf Bourguignon
description: Beef braised slowly in red wine with bacon, then finished with browned mushrooms and glazed small onions. Julia Child, co-author of Mastering the Art of French Cooking (1961), cooked it on the first regular episode of her television show The French Chef in February 1963.
notes:
Inspired by Julia Child, *Mastering the Art of French Cooking* (1961). Written for Sous; not her recipe.

Make it a day ahead if you can: the flavour settles overnight, and the fat sets on top of the cold stew so you can lift it off. Reheat covered in a 325°F (165°C) oven for about 45 minutes, or gently on the stove.

Use a wine you would happily drink; a Pinot Noir or Côtes du Rhône is plenty. Frozen pearl onions work well and save the peeling.
ingredients: 6 ounces (170 g) slab bacon or pancetta, cut into 1/4-inch-thick strips
3 1/2 pounds (1.6 kg) boneless beef chuck, cut into 2-inch (5 cm) chunks
2 teaspoons kosher salt, plus more to taste
2 cups (480 ml) beef or chicken stock
4 sprigs thyme, 4 parsley stems and 1 bay leaf, tied with string
20 to 24 pearl onions, peeled, or 10 ounces (285 g) frozen, thawed
Boiled potatoes, buttered egg noodles or crusty bread, for serving
steps: Heat the oven to 325°F (165°C) with a rack in the lower third. Pat the beef very dry and season with the salt and pepper.
Cook the bacon in a large Dutch oven over medium heat until browned and the fat has rendered, 6 to 8 minutes. Lift it out with a slotted spoon and set aside.

Add the oil to the bacon fat and raise the heat to medium-high. Brown the beef in three batches without crowding, turning until well browned on at least two sides, 8 to 10 minutes per batch. Move each batch to a plate.

Pour off all but about 2 tablespoons of fat. Lower the heat to medium, add the carrot and onion, and cook, stirring, until softened and lightly browned, 6 to 8 minutes. Stir in the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute, then sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute more.

Pour in the wine, scraping up every browned bit from the bottom. Add the stock, the herb bundle, the beef with its juices and the bacon. The liquid should come most of the way up the meat; add a little water if needed.
Bring to a simmer on the stove, cover, and move to the oven. Braise until a piece of beef breaks apart easily with a fork, 2 1/2 to 3 hours.

While the beef braises, melt 1 tablespoon of the butter in a skillet over medium heat. Add the onions and roll them around until lightly browned, about 8 minutes. Add the water and a pinch of salt, cover, and simmer until tender, 15 to 20 minutes, then uncover and cook until the liquid has reduced to a glaze. Set aside.

Wipe out the skillet, raise the heat to medium-high, and melt the remaining 2 tablespoons butter. Brown the mushrooms in two batches, leaving them alone for the first few minutes so they colour, 6 to 8 minutes per batch. Season with salt.
Lift the beef and bacon into a bowl with a slotted spoon and discard the herb bundle (the carrot and onion can stay in the sauce or be strained out). Skim the fat from the sauce.
Simmer the sauce on the stove until it coats the back of a spoon, 5 to 10 minutes. Taste for salt and pepper.
Return the beef and bacon to the pot with the onions and mushrooms and warm through gently for 5 minutes. Scatter with parsley and serve with potatoes, noodles or bread.
